title: SGLang custom logit processor dill deserialization permits remote code execution
ai_system: Antiproof AI-powered vulnerability discovery system (specific model not identified)
organization: Antiproof / SGLang maintainers (no vendor response recorded by CERT/CC)
summary: The serving runtime deserializes a hex-encoded dill payload in the custom_logit_processor field without validation. Antiproof reports unauthenticated code execution when --enable-custom-logit-processor is enabled and a generation endpoint is reachable; it says the option is off by default.
ai_role: The Antiproof article identifies this CVE among three findings it disclosed on 2026-03-10. Antiproof’s AI-system page explicitly includes CVE-2026-7304 among the system’s autonomously discovered and validated cases. The sources do not identify a specific model or separately describe model steps for this issue. CERT/CC independently records the dill deserialization and conditional RCE impact.
classification_note: Public disclosure is documented by the Antiproof report and CERT/CC note. The checked sources do not establish exploitation in the wild; disclosure status does not imply it was or was not a zero-day.
remediation_note: Antiproof and CERT/CC report no official patch as of 2026-05-15 and 2026-05-18 respectively. Current remediation or fixed release boundary was not established by these checks.

impacts.conditions: Unauthenticated remote code execution as the SGLang process user, conditional on the custom logit processor option being enabled and a generation endpoint being reachable.
impacts.exploitation: The cited sources describe vulnerability capability and conditions; they do not report observed exploitation in the wild.
